sections.heading: The Forensic Psych Record Review Problem
paragraphs: Forensic psychiatric and psychological evaluations are built on the record. Competency, criminal responsibility, psychological damages in civil cases, disability opinions, fitness-for-duty determinations, custody evaluations — every referral question sits on top of a psychiatric history that often spans decades. Intake notes from a dozen therapists, discharge summaries from three or four hospitalizations, medication trials that changed every few months, ER visits, involuntary holds, substance use treatment records, school and military records touching mental status.

You can't skim this material. A missed prior hospitalization can undo a competency opinion at cross. A missed medication trial can change your causation analysis. So you read it all, and pre-eval prep quietly eats an entire day per case.

Dodonai's {{link:/ai-medical-record-summaries-chronologies/|AI medical chronologies}} were built for this. Upload the entire record set — decades of outpatient notes, inpatient stays, pharmacy records, ER visits — and Dodonai returns a structured psychiatric chronology with every diagnosis dated, every psychotropic medication trial extracted with prescriber and duration, every prior hospitalization surfaced with admission date, length of stay, and discharge diagnosis. Each finding cites back to its source page so you verify before you cite the record in a report.
You still form the opinion. Dodonai just does the mechanical reading that keeps you from getting to the opinion.

faq.question: Can Dodonai handle a record set that spans 20+ years of psychiatric treatment?
faq.answer: Yes. A record set covering decades of outpatient notes, multiple hospitalizations, and years of medication trials is chronologized in minutes, and every finding cites back to the source page so you can verify what you plan to cite in your report.

faq.question: Does the AI accurately extract medication trials and prior hospitalizations?
faq.answer: Yes. Psychotropic medication trials are pulled with prescriber, dosage, duration, and documented reason for discontinuation where available. Prior inpatient stays, involuntary holds, and ER psychiatric visits are surfaced with admission and discharge dates, length of stay, and discharge diagnosis. You can verify any entry against the source page in one click.

faq.question: Can I focus the chronology around a specific referral question?
faq.answer: Yes. You can tailor the output to the question in front of you — competency, criminal responsibility, psychological damages, disability, fitness for duty — so the chronology surfaces what's relevant. Reusable templates via {{link:/dodonai-extract-and-draft-agents/|Extract and Draft Agents}} let you save your preferred structure per evaluation type.

faq.question: Is Dodonai secure enough for sensitive forensic mental health records?
faq.answer: Forensic mental health PHI is among the most sensitive material in medicine, and the platform is built for that standard. A signed BAA is available on request, SOC 2 certified infrastructure, AES-256 encryption on every file. Records never enter a training pipeline, and deletion runs on your schedule.

faq.question: Can the AI handle handwritten intake notes and older paper records?
faq.answer: Yes. Dodonai's {{link:/ai-pdf-ocr/|AI OCR engine}} processes handwritten therapist notes, scanned admission records, and faxed hospital discharges. Older paper records and low-quality scans are handled without a separate OCR step.

faq.question: What does it cost to run a typical forensic evaluation record set?
faq.answer: Per-page pricing. Even the multi-thousand-page files common in serious forensic work run a small fraction of manual review time and outsourced summarization vendor rates. See {{link:/pricing/|pricing}} for current rates.
